subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw core own pace-aware autonomous throttling, and what minimal first phase should ship?
rationale: The remaining work would add provider-specific usage semantics, persisted state, new agent config, and autonomous throttling behavior, so source inspection cannot choose the product/API contract safely.

options.title: Visibility-Only Pace First
options.body: Capture or derive pace context for status and session_status without blocking work until provider semantics and data reliability are proven.

options.title: Full Opt-In Throttling Policy
options.body: Add disabled-by-default pace thresholds that can throttle subagents or non-interactive work, with explicit config, tests, docs, and recovery behavior.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Resource Governance
options.body: Make this part of the broader rate-limit, provider-pool, and budget governance trackers rather than a standalone Anthropic-paced core feature.

recommendation.title: Visibility-Only Pace First
recommendation.body: Capture or derive pace context for status and session_status without blocking work until provider semantics and data reliability are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The current usage/status surfaces and adjacent auth/provider policy history point most strongly to steipete for deciding the core product boundary.
